tier_reason: The README feature line gives only first-party summary ratios against Zend PHP (~2.5x faster than PHP 5.6, ~1.1x faster than PHP 7.0, ~13% slower than PHP 7.4). Benchmark scripts are public (bench/src/bench.php with ~22 micro-benchmarks, run via ./gradlew bench), but no per-benchmark numbers, JVM or PHP build details, or hardware are given, so C.
notes: Numbers and metadata check out (Apache-2.0, 1.7k stars, last commit 2020-07-07 on master, not archived, so abandoned). Shortcoming: slower than PHP 7.4 by its own README and predates PHP 8 and its JIT, so it beats only obsolete Zend versions; ratios only, no per-benchmark data, hardware or flags.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C. The harness is public (tamnd/katsu-bench src/ and workloads/, command 'katsu-bench run --runs 25', committed table results/baselines/2026-08-29-m4-macos.md). The compiler is pinned (rust-toolchain.toml channel 1.98.0, the same at tag v0.0.5), release flags are in katsu's Cargo.toml [profile.release] (opt-level 3, lto fat, codegen-units 1, panic abort), the CPU is named (Apple M4, macOS 15.8), and the rivals are named official releases (Node 26.8.1, Bun 1.4.0, Deno 2.9.6).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.98.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml (also at tag v0.0.5); cargo --release with Cargo.toml [profile.release] opt-level=3, lto="fat", codegen-units=1, panic="abort", strip="symbols"; 0.0.5 measured from a local release build, 0.1.2 onwards from the published tarballs; Node 26.8.1, Bun 1.4.0 and Deno 2.9.6 are their official release binaries
corrections.hardware: Apple M4 (10 cores, 24 GB), macOS 15.8 (Darwin 15.8), a laptop with turbo and frequency scaling not pinned (numbers labelled 'indicative' by spec 15.5)
corrections.workload: Wall-clock cold start (spawn to exit) of a one-line console.log hello world, 25 runs per runtime, median and IQR (spec 15.5.1 says no warmup for startup; the katsu-bench README says 25 runs after 3 discarded), plus peak RSS from a separate /usr/bin/time -l pass and distribution size (executable plus non-system shared libraries).
corrections.claimed_speedup: Cold start (spec 15.5.1, katsu 0.0.5): katsu 1.55 ms vs Node 26.8.1 24.63 ms (page: 15.9x faster), Bun 1.4.0 4.97 ms (3.2x), Deno 2.9.6 12.49 ms; peak RSS 2.44 MiB vs 48.14 MiB for Node (19.7x) and 10.92 MiB for Bun (4.5x); binary 1.7 MiB vs 139.0 MiB for Node (80x). The lead holds in later katsu-bench runs (0.1.8: 1.68 ms vs Bun 5.67 ms, 3.37x ahead). Compute is a loss: katsu README fib(35) 875 ms vs Node 53.4 ms, Bun 34.3 ms and Deno 56.5 ms (16.4x slower than Node, 25.5x slower than Bun, 0.1.6 baseline); katsu-bench shows fib 19-25x behind Bun across 0.1.3-0.1.8.

notes: Numbers match spec/15-benchmarks.md and the katsu-bench baseline file exactly. Metadata checks out: MIT OR Apache-2.0, 0 stars, 67 commits, last commit 2026-08-31, so active. Shortcomings: by the author's own statement the startup and memory lead exists because katsu does less (no module system, event loop, process, Buffer or GC; it is an interpreter with an inline cache, not yet a JIT), compute is 16-25x slower than Node and Bun, and numbers come from a laptop with turbo on and are labelled indicative. A by the letter of the rubric (public harness, pinned compiler, flags and CPU); the orchestrator may prefer to note the feature gap prominently.

tier_reason: The README Benchmarks table matches the record exactly (10 tasks, all won against LuaJ 3.0.1). The harness is public (benchmarks/harness/interleave.sh, Bench.java, LuaJBench.java: paired, order-flipped, taskset-pinned, java -XX:+UseG1GC -Xmx1g), but no CPU model or exact JDK version is stated and the README numbers have no committed results file, so C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: JDK 21+ (exact JDK build not stated); harness benchmarks/harness/interleave.sh runs java -XX:+UseG1GC -Xmx1g with -Dluava.jit.sync=true, taskset-pinned to one core except the coroutine task; LuaJ 3.0.1 run through LuaJBench.java with the same flags
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers with no CPU model and no committed results file for the README table; benchmarks/harness/BASELINE.txt (2026-09-14, before the JIT) had Luava behind LuaJ on 5 of 10 tasks, so the wins come from the newer tiered JIT. LuaJ interprets Lua 5.2 semantics while Luava implements 5.4, so the tasks are not exactly equivalent. Both harnesses re-evaluate the source each iteration (loadfile/eval), and every task asserts its result. Neither PUC Lua nor LuaJIT appears in the current table: the committed benchmarks/results/benchmark_report_20260911_201214.md (an early pre-JIT build) shows Luava 4x to 114x slower than C Lua 5.4. benchmarks/harness/FINDINGS.txt records C Lua 5.4.9 fib(35) at ~766 ms against a ~190 ms JIT spike on the same box, so the current JIT may beat C Lua on fib, but no head-to-head with the shipped JIT is published. Cold start is a loss: the first eval of a small script takes ~47 ms against LuaJ's 13 ms. The coroutine win (19.4x) reflects virtual threads against LuaJ's platform-thread coroutines. MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft. Very small project (52 commits, 2 stars).

notes: Numbers and metadata check out: MPL-2.0, 2 stars, 52 commits, release 0.2.5 on Maven Central, last commit 2026-09-29 on master, so active. Shortcomings: baseline is the slow LuaJ interpreter rather than PUC Lua or LuaJIT; no hardware; the repo's own committed report against C Lua (pre-JIT) shows Luava much slower; first-eval cold start loses to LuaJ.
